rows.notes: Unexpected low score root cause: The run was completed voluntarily and produced a substantial C++ implementation (~3K nonblank LOC, 10 published files) that built successfully, but it failed the eval largely because its observable JSON contract did not match the test suite. It emitted axis values as arrays instead of {x,y,z,a,b,c} objects, used g_modal/m_modal instead of active_modal_g_codes/active_modal_m_codes, used coord_system_offsets instead of coordinate_system_offsets, emitted lowercase spindle directions, and omitted the required top-level error string on failing inputs. These schema issues alone caused broad failures across position tracking, modal state, output schema, error, and trace suites. Additional semantic gaps were incomplete cutter-radius compensation (CRC arcs explicitly unsupported and corner lookahead skipped), trace entries using source_line/position instead of line_number/machine_position with missing top-level trace error fields, weak invalid-input validation (duplicate A/B/C accepted, noninteger D/H rounded, negative spindle speed accepted, some invalid TLO/tool/G53/linear-motion cases accepted), missing canned-cycle P/negative-P checks, simplified probing behavior, and parameter output that only wrote nonzero params instead of the required parameter set. The agent's final 'fully functional' claim is therefore grossly overstated, but the failure is not no_code_written or near-empty code; it is a substantial implementation with major public-contract and edge-case completeness failures.

rows.notes: Unexpected low score root cause: The run completed voluntarily, built successfully, and had complete Codex token/cost data, so there is no infra/auth/rate-limit/timeout issue. It produced a substantial C++ implementation/wrapper (published source_stats: 7 files / 14104 LOC; transient source includes main.cpp plus canonical rs274ngc files), but the dominant failure is an eval contract mismatch: main.cpp rejects any non-percent-delimited program that does not end in M2/M30 with 'file ended without M2/M30 and without percent demarcation'. The RS274 tests intentionally use many valid snippet programs without program end markers. As a result, 262 of 283 failures are valid-input tests failing at completed.returncode == 0 before state assertions, which wipes out modal state, position tracking, canned cycles, cutter-radius compensation, parameter expressions, probing, and much of trace. Secondary shortcomings remain even when programs do end: parameter-output files are not reliably written and required parameters are missing, trace initial_state does not preserve loaded parameters, nonmodal G-code labels and submotion stepping are wrong for G28/G30/G92/G4/canned-cycle cases, and CRC/probing/trace edge behavior is incomplete. The low score is legitimate and reflects a substantial implementation with a wrong snippet-acceptance contract plus incomplete peripheral semantics, not no_code_written, build failure, or infrastructure.
rows.last_message: Claims complete; built successfully; low score is legitimate: rejects valid snippet programs without M2/M30/%.
